ai.description: This stout-bodied snake reaches 60–100 cm. It is grey or olive with dark, narrow crossbands and a distinctively broad, triangular head. Its eyes are positioned dorsally with vertically elliptical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The South Asian Bockadam is best distinguished by its strongly keeled scales and a distinct, dark stripe running through each eye, which separates it from similar water snakes.
ai.habitat: The South Asian Bockadam inhabits coastal mangroves, tidal creeks, and estuaries, often found among *Avicennia* and *Rhizophora* vegetation at low elevations.
ai.behavior: The South Asian Bockadam is primarily nocturnal and utilizes a "loop-and-snap" hunting strategy, anchoring its body to mangrove roots to ambush passing fish.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cerberus rynchops* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 8–30 young. In India, breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cerberus rynchops occurs in coastal areas of India, primarily along the eastern seaboard in West Bengal, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh, inhabiting mangroves and estuaries.
